The '''2003–04 Scottish Premier League''' was won by [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].

As league [[champions]], Celtic qualified for the UEFA Champions League group stage, with [[runner-up|runners-up]] [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] also qualifying to the third qualifying round. Third-placed [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] qualified for the [[UEFA Cup]], as did [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], who took the [[Scottish Cup]] place despite losing the final to Celtic.

During the season, Celtic set a Scottish record of 25 successive wins.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/2008/12/02/celtic-tipped-to-break-2004-25-game-winning-streak-by-mjallby-86908-20940079/ |title=Celtic tipped to break 2004 25-game winning streak by Mjallby |newspaper=The Daily Record |access-date=29 December 2010}}</ref>

[[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] were relegated, and [[Scottish First Division|First Division]] winners [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] were promoted.

Celtic's [[Henrik Larsson]] was the top scorer with 30 goals.

==Teams==
===Promotion and relegation from 2002–03===
[[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] finished bottom of the [[2002–03 Scottish Premier League]] but were spared relegation, as [[2002–03 Scottish First Division]] champions [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] were denied promotion due to their lack of an appropriate stadium for the [[Scottish Premier League]].
